title: SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) - n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz 5G NR) for UWB (Ultra-Wideband) Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Stefan Richter

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) filter targeting n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz 5G NR) for UWB (Ultra-Wideband) Filter. The filter is designed on AlN on SiC substrate with a target center frequency of 2088.4 MHz and bandwidth of 328.4 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the UWB (Ultra-Wideband) Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave)
- Frequency Band: n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz 5G NR)
- Application: UWB (Ultra-Wideband) Filter
- Substrate: AlN on SiC
- Package: Fan-Out WLP
- Design Tool: Keysight ADS 2024
- Design Center: Osaka Design Center

This specification applies to all variants of the SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) design targeting n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz 5G NR). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       2088.4 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       328.4 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 3.4 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 21.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 40.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 44.0 dB
Q Factor:               9997
Temperature Coefficient:-23.1 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.7 x 1.8 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   4
Electrode Material:     Mo
Passivation:            SiO2/Si3N4 stack
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Keysight ADS 2024 and load the SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: AlN on SiC with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 2088.4 MHz, BW 328.4 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 3.4 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (Fan-Out WLP).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, AlN on SiC).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Keysight N5227B PNA.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 6265 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 3.4 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 21.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 493 MHz offset >= 40.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 2 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 6.0 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +29 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 500 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 88%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2025-06-10
Devices Tested:         24
Insertion Loss (meas):  3.09 dB
Return Loss (meas):     23.4 dB
Rejection (meas):       42.7 dB
Isolation (meas):       48.5 dB
Q Factor (meas):        9997
Group Delay Variation:  1.8 ns
Power Handling:         +35 dBm
Die Yield:              92.0%

Result Classification:  FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) design demonstrated below-target performance for n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz 5G NR).
b) Insertion loss is marginally above target; electrode thickness optimization recommended.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Slight frequency drift observed at +85°C; TC layer thickness may need adjustment.
e) ESD robustness exceeded specification by 2x margin.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Optimize resonator geometry to reduce insertion loss by ~0.3 dB.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Escalate to advanced materials team for alternative piezoelectric stack.
